messages.author: 334c7505e0b5cf65
messages.subject: Re-fitting model and model.matrix
parts:
Dear all,

I am fitting a large model (~7K fixed effects) with INLA to some images on handwritten digits. So far, I have tried the model on a subset of the complete dataset but I would like to use the complete  dataset (or, at least, a larger subset). For this, I have the following questions:

- Can I re-fit a model using a previously fitted model? I know I can use 

control.mode = list(results = some.results)

but I am not sure whether this will work if I increase the number of observed data as model.matrix will certainly change (but not the number of effects in theta and x).

The reason is to make the model with the new dataset to fit faster than the previous one as the estimates will be very similar.

- The matrix in ...$model.matrix takes more than 2Gb but if converted into a (sparse) Matrix it only takes 72Mb. Is there a way of telling inla to use sparse matrices here.

Many thanks!

Virgilio

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re-fitting model and model.matrix
parts:
> On 18 Dec 2016, at 15:59, Virgilio Gómez Rubio <becario...@gmail.com> wrote:
> - Can I re-fit a model using a previously fitted model? I know I can use
>
> control.mode = list(results = some.results)
>
> but I am not sure whether this will work if I increase the number of observed data as model.matrix will certainly change (but not the number of effects in theta and x).

In this situation you need to supply only the part that is common between the the two runs, which is the hyper parameter vector:
control.mode=list(theta=some.results$mode$theta)

Finn

messages.author: 334c7505e0b5cf65
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re-fitting model and model.matrix
parts:
Hi Finn,

Many thanks for your reply.

In this situation you need to supply only the part that is common between the the two runs, which is the hyper parameter vector:
control.mode=list(theta=some.results$mode$theta)

OK. I am doing:

system.time(m3 <- inla(m.form,  data = d2, family = rep("binomial", n.grp),
  control.fixed = list(expand.factor.strategy='inla'),
  control.mode = list(theta = m2$mode$theta, x = m2$mode$x, restart = TRUE)
))

But the model takes a similar time to run (on exactly the same dataset). I was expecting that by including estimates of the modes the model would fit faster... I also tried with restart = FALSE (the default) with a similar computation time...

Best,

Virgilio

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re-fitting model and model.matrix
parts:
As usual, please run with verbose=TRUE. That will show if the optimizer is converging sensibly and faster in the second run than in the first (when restart=TRUE) and if the integration step is the time consuming part (in both cases). Your comment seems to indicate the latter.

Finn

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re-fitting model and model.matrix
parts:
On Sun, 2016-12-18 at 16:59 +0100, Virgilio Gómez Rubio wrote:
>
> - Can I re-fit a model using a previously fitted model? I know I can
> use 
>
> control.mode = list(results = some.results)

yes. I would also add

restart=TRUE

otherwise, you'll fix \theta.

results=r will initialise both \theta and the latent model x. if you
change the dimension of 'x' through increasing number of data, you can
initialise just \theta by

control.mode = list(theta = r$mode$theta, restart=TRUE)

for which 'x' is initialized by the default initilizer. otherwise it
will throw and error.

> - The matrix in ...$model.matrix takes more than 2Gb but if converted
> into a (sparse) Matrix it only takes 72Mb. Is there a way of telling
> inla to use sparse matrices here.
>

good question. I think we never seen a such case with so many
fixed.effs. I'll look into the code...

H

parts:
Just to chime in:

If you add "control.inla=list(verbose=T)", you will see the x-optimisation. INLA only requires several steps (on x) in the first evaluation of the posterior. Hence, adding the initial value for x is only used once in the ca 100+ evaluations of the posterior for theta that is needed for the optimiser.

Attached is an example logfile,
Haakon
